unrefuted.quote: the line is chosen to fit the estimates as well as possible, a null that is adversarial toward finding pre-trend violations.
unrefuted.what_is_wrong: The null is stated correctly, and the author ruled it (BS-12, one-parameter line through the reference). The interpretation is what fails. The option is called the 'adversarial pre-trend test' in every message, and the help frames it as a pre-trend diagnostic. But its null covers the POST-treatment coefficients too: the whole event-study path, pre and post, lies on one line through the reference. So any genuine treatment effect that does not happen to continue a line rejects it. The probe shows this: on dta_binary, with flat pre-trends (joint pre-trend p = .75 and .81) and a real effect, the adversarial p is 5e-14. A reader who takes a small 'adversarial pre-trend' p as a detected pre-trend violation draws the wrong inference. Nothing in the help or the guide says that rejection is expected whenever there is a real effect, or how to read the test beside jointtests. The guide copy at line 451 has the same sentence.
unrefuted.correct_statement: The null is what a linear differential trend with no treatment effect would produce: every coefficient, pre and post, lies on one line through the reference period. A small p says no such line fits. A genuine treatment effect produces that, and so does a pre-trend that is not linear, so a rejection is not evidence of a pre-trend violation. Read it beside the joint pre-trend test. If the joint test rejects and the adversarial test does not, the pre-period coefficients show a clean linear trend that could, by itself, account for the post-treatment estimates.
unrefuted.proposed_fix: sthlp 566: replace 'a null that is adversarial toward finding pre-trend violations.' with 'a null under which a linear pre-trend alone explains every estimate, pre and post. A small p-value says that no such line fits: a genuine treatment effect produces one, and so does a pre-trend that is not linear, so it is not evidence of a pre-trend violation. Read it beside {it:jointtests}: a joint pre-trend rejection with no adversarial rejection points to a linear pre-trend that could account for the post-treatment estimates.' Guide 451: the same sentences in Markdown, replacing 'a null that is adversarial toward finding pre-trend violations in that the slope is chosen to fit the estimates as well as possible'.
unrefuted.reference: Rambachan and Roth (2023), Review of Economic Studies 90(5), the smoothness class Delta^SD(M) at M = 0, which is exactly linear extrapolation of the pre-trend. Dobkin, Finkelstein, Kluender and Notowidigdo (2018), American Economic Review 108(2), the parametric event study with a linear pre-trend. The author's own research record review_process/research_2026-09-08/adversarial_null.md, around line 57, states the pair reading.
unrefuted.ruling_checked: rulings_2026-09-07.md s.J (BS-12: the one-parameter null adopted) and PS-19 ('the adversarial p keeps its placement and label'). These rule the NULL and its label, not the interpretive sentence. research_2026-09-08/adversarial_null.md: 'joint pre-trend rejects but adversarial does not means ... a clean linear pre-trend through the reference period'. That reading is not in the help or the guide (grep 'linear pre-trend|rejects but|adversarial.*reject' over both files finds nothing).
unrefuted.code_site: wooldid.ado 16004-16060 (wooldid_advW alt==0: W = residual quadratic form over ALL event-study coefficients, pre and post)

unrefuted.quote: | `simultaneousbands` | sup-t band over a family's horizons | two horizons with variance | none; unavailable under `fastnose` | `permute()` |
unrefuted.what_is_wrong: The 'not calibrated when' column says 'none'. Without bootstrap(), the band is simulated from e(V_es_*) (wooldid_esbanda: it studentizes that covariance to a correlation matrix and scales by its diagonal). So the band is only as good as that covariance. The help itself says (sthlp 313-315) that with cluster() at or above i the att rows' analytic standard errors are understated without a caution, and the band inherits that understatement in both its width and its critical value. wooldid_esband has no cluster gate and prints no caution. The help's own band entry (sthlp 299, 'which covers every horizon of the family at once with that probability') makes the same unqualified coverage claim. A user who sees 'none' next to jointtests and adversarial rows that list the cluster-at-i condition will take the band as the safe tool in exactly the design where it under-covers.
unrefuted.correct_statement: The analytic sup-t band has its nominal simultaneous coverage only if e(V_es_*) is a consistent estimate of the event-study covariance. With analytic cluster() at or above i, or with singleton treated cells, it under-covers just as the pointwise intervals do, and nothing cautions. The bootstrap band does not read that matrix.
unrefuted.proposed_fix: guide 427: replace 'none; unavailable under `fastnose`' with 'analytic `cluster()` at or above `i`, and singleton treated cells: the band is simulated from `e(V_es_*)` and inherits its understatement, uncautioned. Unavailable under `fastnose`'. sthlp 301, after 'Without {it:bootstrap()} the band is simulated from the family's analytic event study covariance.', add: 'It is then only as good as that covariance: with {it:cluster()} at or above {it:i} it is too narrow, as the pointwise intervals are, and no caution prints. Use {it:bootstrap()} there.'
unrefuted.reference: Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Moller (2019), 'Simultaneous confidence bands: theory, implementation, and an application to SVARs', Journal of Applied Econometrics 34(1): sup-t coverage requires a consistent estimator of the coefficients' covariance.
unrefuted.ruling_checked: grep 'simultaneous|PS-45|esband' in held_for_ruling_2026-09-09.md (PS-45: percentile-t under boottstat, built), changes_review_2026-09-22.md (esband t-law, floor removed, both ruled), and blue_sky_2026-09-18/RULINGS_LEDGER.md (BAND-2b, no heuristic floor). None of these rules on cautioning or documenting the band under cluster at or above i. The no-floor convention is ruled and is not challenged here.
unrefuted.lens: event study, pre-trends, adversarial test and bands

unrefuted.quote: *e(vce)* is *cluster*, *robust*, *unconditional*, *bootstrap*, the first word of `customvce()`, or *ols* (*oim* under `poisson`) when none of those applies
unrefuted.code_site: wooldidinstall/wooldid.ado:5101 (else ereturn local vce = cond("`poisson'" == "poisson", "oim", "ols")); header at ado:12800 prints the empty `vcespecifier'
unrefuted.what_is_wrong: The fallthrough that posts e(vce)=oim is reached under poisson only on the ppmlhdfe path. Unconditionalse and customvce() post their own labels earlier, so the Stata-poisson path never gets here. ppmlhdfe turns an unadjusted request into robust (ppmlhdfe.ado:216, "PPML uses robust SEs") and posts e(vce)=robust itself. So a poisson run without robust or cluster() reports heteroskedasticity-robust sandwich standard errors but labels them oim, posts no e(vcetype), and prints a blank 'Standard Errors:' header. esttab/estout and outreg2 read e(vcetype) to decide the footer, so a paper would describe robust QMLE standard errors as model-based ML standard errors that assume equidispersion. Probe probes/econ_poisson/p1.do: no-vce run gives e(vce)=oim, e(vcetype) empty, se_att=.08589712. The same run with robust gives e(vce)=robust, e(vcetype)=Robust and se_att=.08589712, bit-identical. ppmlhdfe called directly posts robust/Robust. The guide documents the mislabel as if it were correct. The same line also causes the open pweight mislabel FW-02/EC-6 (a pweighted linear run labelled ols).
unrefuted.correct_statement: On the ppmlhdfe path without cluster(), robust or customvce(), the variance is the Poisson QMLE heteroskedasticity-robust sandwich. e(vce) should read robust and e(vcetype) Robust.
unrefuted.proposed_fix: Code (ado:5101): replace the fallthrough with `else if ("`poisson'" == "poisson") | "`weight'" == "pweight" { ereturn local vce robust  ereturn local vcetype Robust }` followed by `else ereturn local vce ols`. The poisson arm is safe because this branch is reached only on the ppmlhdfe path. Also have the header show vce(robust) on that path. Guide :889 becomes: "*e(vce)* is *cluster*, *robust*, *unconditional*, *bootstrap*, the first word of `customvce()`, or *ols* when none of those applies. Under `poisson` without `cluster()` or `customvce()`, *ppmlhdfe* always computes a robust variance, so *e(vce)* is *robust* and *e(vcetype)* is *Robust*."
unrefuted.reference: Gourieroux, Monfort and Trognon (1984), Econometrica 52(3): Poisson QMLE is consistent under mean misspecification of the variance only with the sandwich covariance. Wooldridge (1999), J. Econometrics 90. ppmlhdfe.ado:216. Stata [R] poisson: vce(oim) is the model-based information matrix.
unrefuted.ruling_checked: grep -rn oim review_process: only review_process/blue_sky_2026-09-18/fixprop/proposals_VCV.md:297,320 and repro/agents/fw-weights/FINDINGS.md:241. Those quote the line while rewriting the unconditionalse arm (SKEP-01) and carry the oim branch over without examining it. grep FW-02/EC-6: all_findings.md:209,310 list the sibling pweight mislabel as PARTIAL, with no ruling in changes_review_2026-09-22.md, held_for_ruling_*.md or rulings_2026-09-07.md. Not ruled.

unrefuted.quote: with {it:cluster()} at the level of {it:i} or coarser a treated cell lies inside a single cluster, and under {it:robust}, pweights or a robust {it:customvce()} a cell may hold a single observation; either way its standard error is understated, which a caution reports
unrefuted.code_site: wooldidinstall/wooldid.ado:2368 (gteffects containment screen, observation branch keyed on `robust', pweight, customvce robust/hc2/hc3); also ado:2107 (ame not-identified caution offers 'conditional robust standard errors' whenever `robust' is empty)
unrefuted.what_is_wrong: The single-observation containment screen for e(gteffects) arms only when the user typed robust, used pweights, or gave a robust customvce(). On the default poisson path ppmlhdfe computes the same heteroskedasticity-robust variance without being asked (ppmlhdfe.ado:216), and `robust' stays empty (ado:1924). So a poisson gteffects run on a fine-i design reports understated cell standard errors and intervals with no caution and no e(gt_ncontained). The help says a caution reports this. Mechanism: the cell dummy fits a one-row cell exactly, the Poisson residual there is zero, and the robust meat gets nothing from the cell. Probe p1.do (40 units, i = unit, 8 periods): without a vce option there is no caution. Adding robust gives identical numbers plus 'Caution: 80 of 80 e(gteffects) cell(s) lie wholly inside a single observation'. A second site has the same keying: at ado:2107 the ame not-identified caution suggests 'conditional robust standard errors' to a poisson-default run that already has them (message text, so it needs the author's clearance).
unrefuted.correct_statement: Under poisson on the ppmlhdfe path the variance is always robust. Single-observation treated cells there have understated coefficient-level standard errors, exactly as under robust, and the screen should fire.
unrefuted.proposed_fix: Code (ado:2368): add `| ("`poisson'" == "poisson" & "`unconditionalse'" == "" & "`customvce'" == "")` to the observation-branch condition. At ado:2107, treat that same poisson case as already robust when building `wdr4alt'. Help :907: "...and under {it:robust}, pweights, a robust {it:customvce()} or {it:poisson} without {it:cluster()} (which {it:ppmlhdfe} always estimates with a robust variance) a cell may hold a single observation; either way its standard error is understated, which a caution reports;". Make the same change to the guide's copy at :921.
unrefuted.reference: Chesher and Jewitt (1987), Econometrica 55(5): the HC0 variance with a regressor that isolates one observation has a zero residual there and is biased down. MacKinnon and White (1985). ppmlhdfe.ado:216.
unrefuted.ruling_checked: grep -rn 'gt_ncontained|wholly inside a single' review_process: blue_sky_2026-09-18/fix_proposal_status.md:400-430 (the GTE containment proposal). The reviewers there found and closed the customvce(robust) and hc2 holes, but no row mentions poisson. amese/R1_design_note.md:18 concerns cluster containment only. No ruling on the poisson case.

deletion_lenses.lens: User value: how often a competent applied economist running a staggered DiD would need the feature, whether another option, the stored e() results or an external package (honestdid, pretrends, ritest, bayesboot) already gives the same result, and whether the feature makes the help harder to use. That is weighed against the code, message, doc and test burden it carries. Working notes: /var/folders/ls/yldcbdg94wq_f401f_nynbsc0000gn/T/wooldid_e098/review/notes/delete_value.md. Stata probes (one instance each, on test/data/dta_binary.dta): /var/folders/ls/yldcbdg94wq_f401f_nynbsc0000gn/T/wooldid_e098/review/probes/delete_value/probe.log and probe2.log. The v1.3 tag was checked for each candidate: the permute() knobs, bootalpha() and pretrendpower() are not in v1.3, so removing them breaks no do-file written for the last tagged release; altmethod_adversarial, cleanmatrices, emptycellsoverride and suppresssgprimaryeffects are in v1.3, so removing them is a clean break of the r(198) kind (the fastcollapse precedent, option_consolidation_2026-09-16.md).

candidates.what_it_is: Turns off wooldid's program-scoped `set emptycells drop`, so the underlying regression carries columns for empty interaction cells.

It is a pure help-surface cost: one syntax-table token, one option entry, one runtime sentence and one guide lever.
candidates.burden_evidence: The code is small: the worker gate at wooldid.ado:804-811, forwarding into both replication option strings (ado:221 permute, ado:440 bootstrap), both byte-identical syntax lines (753/5388) and the wdv_ret list (6322). No core suite config, one ext config. Docs: sthlp:911-913 entry, sthlp:941 runtime sentence, the sthlp:110 syntax table, guide ch.11 lever 7. The payoff is surface area, not lines.

It also clears wooldid's own Mata kernels mid-session, which has forced defensive design across the ado and the harness. It forced cap-guards and design workarounds at ado:12371 (esband), 12524 (vsplice) and 14763 (an fcdeg screen written inline 'on purpose' because cleanmatrices would delete a named Mata helper, r(3499)). An option whose only non-default value gives wrong standard errors on the package's core data type should not be on the user surface. With size gone, the option has one value and goes too.

The size branch runs through wooldid_bootrun (comments and divisor logic at ado:9992-10075), the Mata draw kernel wooldid_bootdw (ado:16184-16207), the bootsave() w_ divisor at ado:600, and e(boot_alpha) at ado:11643.
