candidates.what_it_is: A modifier of adversarial that swaps the line test for a forecast test: fit a line to the pre-period coefficients plus the reference, then test the post coefficients jointly against its projection.
candidates.why_delete: It is a second statistic for a diagnostic that is already niche, and it is threaded through every engine. Its question (are post effects distinguishable from a continued linear pre-trend?) is answered better by honestdid's smoothness restriction with M = 0, a robust interval on the post effects rather than a p-value. wooldid already hands honestdid e(b_es_*), e(V_es_*) and e(numpre_*).
candidates.burden_evidence: Parse gate at ado:1231-1238, refusal at ado:6278-6285, a 'gapskip' return status in wooldid_advstat (ado:14385-14397, 14424-14425) that all four call sites must branch on (ado:2795, 3295, 3611, 4076), and a separate Mata forecast branch in wooldid_advW (alt==1, after ado:16060). advalt/alt is threaded into wooldid_permjnt (ado:344), wooldid_bootrun (543), wooldid_bootjnt (587), wooldid_bootsave (600), wooldid_permadv/permadvline and wooldid_bootadvobs. 3 messages. Tests: test_advstat.do, test_advguard.do, test_ptpdisp.do, runbattery.do; 4 core + 2 ext suite configs and the baseline adv_altb.csv. History: the statistic was anti-conservative and its covariance was rebuilt (held_for_ruling_2026-09-13.md s10: pinned p moved from 1.0e-22 to about 3.7e-6).
candidates.value_evidence: Few applied users would pick the forecast variant over the default line test, and the honestdid route answers the same question with an interval. The primary adversarial test stays.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming altmethod_adversarial stops with r(198). The e(adversarial_pval_*) and e(adversarial_line_*) produced under it go; adversarial alone behaves as today.

candidates.what_it_is: Makes the printed permutation p-values one-sided (share at or below, or at or above, the observed statistic).
candidates.why_delete: It is a display toggle for numbers wooldid already posts on every permute() run: e(perm_p_lo) and e(perm_p_hi) are the same one-sided shares under the same add-one/exact rule (ado:9221-9227; the guide says so at guide:397). The interval stays two-sided anyway (rulings_2026-09-07). The family tests ignore it (ado:18302). It adds a fifth convention code to four programs.
candidates.burden_evidence: Validation and a mutual-exclusion refusal at ado:6635-6640, convention codes 3/4 in wooldid_permwire (9007), wooldid_permjnt (9391), wooldid_permcellsx (9841) and wooldid_permtail (after 17987), footer text ado:13170, e(perm_pconv), the pfloor branch. 2 messages. Tests: test_permute3.do (Q25 convention loop), runbattery.do; 1 core config.
candidates.value_evidence: A user who wants a one-sided RI p reads e(perm_p_lo) or e(perm_p_hi), already stored by coefficient name. Cells without those matrices can be rebuilt from e(permdist_b) or permsave().
candidates.what_breaks: The printed p column, e(perm_p) and e(p) (and so esttab) can no longer carry the one-sided p. Users read e(perm_p_lo)/e(perm_p_hi) instead. The continuous-treatment plot cells lose their one-sided variant. Not in v1.3.

candidates.what_it_is: Reports the plain absolute-value share c/n without the add-one adjustment, the number ritest and Stata's permute prefix print.
candidates.why_delete: It differs from permabsp only by the add-one term. The raw form is the anti-conservative one: it can print exactly 0, which Phipson and Smyth argue against for sampled draws. Under permexact the two are identical. Its one use is matching ritest's printed number, which is a one-line conversion from permabsp and e(perm_n).
candidates.burden_evidence: Convention code 2 in wooldid_permtail (ado:17987 onward: out[3] = ma/n vs (1+ma)/(n+1)) and in the four programs listed for permside. A special no-floor, can-print-0 path in wooldid_pfloor (ado:12216) and the footer at ado:13166. The mutual-exclusion refusal at 6639. Tests: test_permute3.do Q22, Q25 and Q28 (BS-25, the exact-0 case); 1 core config.
candidates.value_evidence: Sampled draws: raw = ((n+1)*p_absp - 1)/n with n from e(perm_n). Enumerated: raw = p_absp exactly. ritest and permute themselves remain available for benchmarking.
candidates.what_breaks: Anyone benchmarking against ritest converts by hand, and the printed p is never exactly 0 on sampled draws. Not in v1.3.

candidates.what_it_is: Computes Roth (2022) pre-trend power diagnostics in-run: a GLS pre-trend slope, the minimal detectable linear trend for the Wald and NIS pre-tests at requested power levels, and the implied bias.
candidates.why_delete: It reimplements, in part, what Roth's own pretrends package does. wooldid already posts that package's inputs (e(b_es_*), e(V_es_*), e(numpre_*)), and the help defers to it past 4 pre-periods (mdt_nis is capped there). It is the largest single diagnostic block that duplicates an external tool.
candidates.burden_evidence: wooldid_ptpcheck + wooldid_ptp at ado:11696-12125 (about 430 lines), the replay-only display part(roth) at ado:12913-13001 (about 90 lines), and bootstrap-split glue in the shell (ado:606-615) and worker (5286-5317). A shared nesting caution at ado:1868-1919. About 25 message lines: refusals with impvalues, fastnose, permute, no esfixedbaseperiod and bad levels, plus skip cautions. 13 e() objects (e(roth_*)). Tests: test_ptpdisp.do, test_ptpreplay.do, plus legs in test_bootstrap_gates, test_fastnose, test_level and test_permute3; 2 core configs. Ruled and reworked repeatedly (BS-9 'one statistic one rule' in rulings_2026-09-07; ptp-nis-tcrit-normal-law in the 09-22 review).
candidates.value_evidence: Power analysis of pre-tests is recommended practice, but the standard tool is pretrends, fed from e(b_es_*)/e(V_es_*)/e(numpre_*) with no extra estimation. What wooldid adds that pretrends does not do from those inputs directly is the in-run table and the bootstrap-covariance variant (pretrends can take e(V_es_*) from a bootstrap run too, since that matrix becomes the bootstrap covariance).
candidates.what_breaks: The in-run Roth table and its replay, e(roth_*), and the one-call bootstrap-covariance version. Users run pretrends on the posted event-study vector and covariance. The author built this (F7) and has ruled on it, so it is a real loss of convenience, not just surface. Not in v1.3.

candidates.what_it_is: Under permute(), takes the observed run out of fast mode so the analytic standard errors appear in the se_analytic column and e(V), e(b_es_*) and e(V_es_*) are posted.
candidates.why_delete: Only the observed run leaves fast mode (ado:6195, 6243); the replications stay fast. So every number it adds is exactly what the same specification gives without permute(), a run costing one base fit against the permute run's hundreds. It has also produced a steady stream of defects.
candidates.burden_evidence: 27 ado mentions, 3 messages, a fastnose refusal (built 8443694). Three defects in the 09-22 review: perm-esttab-analytic-under-ase, permute-pairwise-se-analytic-undisclosed and val-permanalyticse-fastnose. A pre-existing permute+contreat+subgroups+ES abort fired only under permanalyticse (blue_sky fix_proposal_status.md:903). Seven test files (test_advstat, test_permute, test_permute3, test_stored, test_sgdegen, test_si7 among them); 2 core configs.
candidates.value_evidence: The analytic SEs, e(V) and the honestdid inputs come from the plain analytic run of the same specification. permtstat, which needs the SEs, keeps computing and showing them.
candidates.what_breaks: Under default permute() the se_analytic column stays blank and no e(V)/e(V_es_*) is posted, so a user wanting both runs twice (or uses permtstat). The permute-then-honestdid path needs the separate analytic run. Not in v1.3.

candidates.what_it_is: Under subgroups(), skips the subgroup-specific estimates and reports only the pairwise subgroup contrasts and the equality tests.
candidates.why_delete: It is a speed knob that both engines refuse, it forks the subgroup code into two output shapes, and it hid a high-severity defect. Since EFF3 the pooled subgroup level margins come free from the pwcompare pass (ado:3398-3404), so the saving is now confined to the per-subgroup event-study and AME passes.
candidates.burden_evidence: 14+ branches in the worker (ado:3393, 3683-3725, 3821, 3868, 4157, 4220, 4380, 4695, 4787, 5131, 5178-5186) plus replay (12780, 13007) and plots (14986, 15147). A hidden e(wdid_suppresssgpe) and an alternate e(wdid_sglev) path that wooldid_sgdeg must read instead of the level tables (ado:12599). Refusals in both engines (ado:6673, 7407). The 09-22 review found sgdeg-inert-under-suppresssg (high; built 637062e). Tests: test_bootstrap_gates, test_permute3, test_sgdegen; 1 ext config.
candidates.value_evidence: Probe S1 (dta_binary, att att_it robust, window 3/3, subgroups(sg)): e(pwsgs) identical, 11.8 s -> 6.6 s. The saving is real, but only on subgroup runs with an event-study window or a continuous treatment. Without one the pooled levels are already free and the option should save little (not measured). fastnose covers the specification-search use case more broadly.
candidates.what_breaks: Users who want only contrasts on large subgroup event-study runs pay roughly the probe's 1.8x. No number changes. A v1.3 do-file naming it stops with r(198).

candidates.feature: Deprecated e() aliases e(perm_lb_est) and e(perm_ub_est)
candidates.what_it_is: Duplicate scalars carrying the same two numbers as e(perm_bandlo_est) and e(perm_bandhi_est), documented in the help as 'deprecated aliases'.
candidates.why_delete: They are documented as deprecated, add a sentence to the longest paragraph in the help (the permutation e() inventory), and duplicate the canonical names exactly. permute() is not in the v1.3 tag, so no do-file written for a tagged release can rely on them.
candidates.burden_evidence: ado:313-314 post them. The footer at ado:13235 still reads the deprecated names and must be switched to perm_bandlo/perm_bandhi. The sentence at sthlp:1105-1106. References in test_permute.do, test_permute3.do and test_stored.do need re-pointing. Tiny, but it is exactly the alias clutter this lens asks about.
candidates.value_evidence: Zero: the canonical scalars hold identical values on every run.
candidates.what_breaks: Code reading e(perm_lb_*)/e(perm_ub_*) gets a missing value and must switch to e(perm_bandlo_*)/e(perm_bandhi_*).

considered_and_kept: permtci: the author already ruled 'Keep it' in changes_review_2026-09-22 (permtci redundant with permtstat permabsp).
latticeignoreweights: the author ruled 'Fix it' on 09-23 and it was built (a977d58); a recent investment, and a user-built xtile variable would not re-bin per bootstrap replication.

ties: probe P2 showed no effect at 99 reps, but with few clusters the identity resample recurs (G!/G^G, 3.8% at G=5) and ties then bites exactly where bootstrap users sit; it is also Stata bootstrap parity per the README design rule; a one-line flag in about a dozen call sites.
update: 5 lines at ado:756-760 with no interactions; it is the package's distribution channel (the blue-sky finding was that a changelog is missing, not that update should go).

customvce(): real burden (it parses cluster variables out of free text at ado:1875, 2070, 2347, 5085), but it is the only route to HC2/HC3 and similar vce types, and the author measured and built its collapse eligibility on 09-22 (cd46002).
cfxplotnose: four rulings and defects on 09-22 show the author engaged with it and chose its engine behaviour; it keeps main-table SEs while skipping the costly plot SEs, which fastnose cannot do.
boot_percentile_mainresults alias: unlike the perm_lb/ub aliases it has a job, making e(boot_`e(boot_display)'_mainresults) derivable under the default display (ado:11160-11167).
histogramcohorteffects: about 125 lines of cheap nose margins (wooldid_hist); the only per-cohort effect output under contreat(), where gteffects is refused.
makecfxplotsbysg: 11 mentions and the natural subgroup extension of cfx plots.
lattice type menu (12 types): about 70 lines of compact xtile/by logic (ado:1273-1337); trimming it saves help text more than code, and users choosing bins need some menu.

ccnoabsorb and ccc_absorb(): stability and memory workarounds bound up with the recently rebuilt poisson paths (v5, 0126d32); ccc_absorb is a different model (i#t#c.x in every cell), not a duplicate of coarsecohortcontrols.

permabsp, permstepdown, permstrata, permprobs, permexact, permonsetcohorts, permsave: design and multiplicity features of randomization inference; permonsetcohorts is what lets the recommended coarse-i, unit-cluster setup use permute().
bootdisplay(bca), bootdf(), boottstat, bootsave(), rseed(), dots(): standard bootstrap surface with clear users.
adversarial (the primary test): heavy (about 31 message lines) but the author's own diagnostic, with rulings on 09-23; only its altmethod variant is proposed.
simultaneousbands: sup-t bands are not available from event_plot or honestdid; modest code.
gteffects: supports custom aggregations and csdid/xthdidregress comparisons.

customweightmultiplier(), oostreatedcontrols(), anticipation(), esrelativeto(), regtol(), verbose, summarystats/escomp, interactivecontrols(), coarsecohortcontrols(), timetrends: core modelling or reporting controls with clear use cases.

deletion_lenses.lens: Maintenance burden: code size, refusal rules and option interactions, engine branches (bootstrap and permute), screens, messages, test legs and battery configs, set against what a competent applied economist loses. Sources: the ado syntax line (753/5388) and the grep-sized branches of each option; the sthlp option entries; the guide ch.14 message table; test/ (excluding suite/out); the author's rulings in review_process (changes_review_2026-09-22, rulings_2026-09-07, blue_sky_2026-09-18/structure_and_ux.md:758-761, which raised seven merge/remove ideas that were never ruled). Working notes: /var/folders/ls/yldcbdg94wq_f401f_nynbsc0000gn/T/wooldid_e098/review/notes/deletion_burden.md. No Stata probe was needed; every claim below is read from code, rulings or stored MC tables.

candidates.what_it_is: A Dirichlet convention for bootstrap(bayes) that gives each cluster a Gamma shape equal to its row count and spreads the drawn mass over its rows, to match the external bayesboot command with id().
candidates.why_delete: By the help's own words the mode exists only to reproduce another tool: 'It is for comparison against that command only; on panel data it understates the standard errors badly.' A switch whose documented job is reproducing an answer known to be wrong on the package's target data is pure cost. Once size is gone, bootalpha(equal) is the only remaining value, so the whole option goes.
candidates.burden_evidence: 28 ado references: a validation block with two errors (ado 7237-7249), the default resolution in bootrun and bootwire (10005, 10908), the size-dependent Gamma shape and the row divisor in Mata wooldid_bootdw (16171-16209, including a 20-line comment defending the divisor), bootsave w_ column semantics, and e(boot_alpha). It has produced three recorded defects: blue-sky bb-02 (the bootsave observed row used the wrong N), HV-BOOT-02 (medium: concentration read off the unscreened frame, which understates the SE further) and a change-audit 09-22 help fix for the w_ column meaning under size. Tests: test_bootstrap_bayes.do, test_bootstrap_gates.do, 3 config rows, mc_bootse.do, analyze_bootse2.py.
candidates.value_evidence: Its only stated user is someone cross-checking against bayesboot. bootalpha(equal), the default, is Rubin's cluster Bayesian bootstrap and is the correct one for panels. A user who wants to match bayesboot can run bayesboot itself.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file typing bootalpha(size) or bootalpha(equal) stops with r(198). No default-path number moves. Tests to retire or edit: the size legs in test_bootstrap_bayes.do and test_bootstrap_gates.do, 3 config rows, and the size arm in mc_bootse.do and analyze_bootse2.py.

candidates.what_it_is: Runs `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` at the start and end of the worker, as folk recovery from a reghdfe failure state.
candidates.why_delete: It destroys the user's own matrices and Mata objects, and it also destroys wooldid's own Mata kernels mid-run. The code has been bent around that in several places and a whole test file exists only for it. The same effect is two commands the user can type before the call.
candidates.burden_evidence: The option itself is 8 lines (ado 797-800, 5350-5353). The code that exists only because of it: (1) the vzero screen uses an inline Mata expression instead of a named function because 'cleanmatrices runs clear mata at the top of the worker, so a named helper is already gone' (ado ~14763); (2) the band and V-splice kernels are cap-wrapped with fallback paths (12371, 12524), so a missing kernel quietly degrades e(V) to the analytic diagonal; (3) the SI-17/SI-18 defects, and a refusal that was built and later removed (test_permute2.do:405-411); (4) all of test/test_adopath.do (134 lines, A0-A3), test_stored.do S9, test_s6.do S5 and the ext_bin_ext_cleanmatrices config; (5) test/suite/mkrun.py:261-271, which isolates every cleanmatrices config in its own shard because one poisons every later config in a do-loaded session. The blue-sky fix proposals also required re-verifying new Mata drops 'under cleanmatrices' (fix_proposal_status.md:201,208).
candidates.value_evidence: The help pitches it as recovery when wooldid 'repeatedly crashes'. The workaround is the same two lines, typed by the user: `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all`, or `discard` and a restart. Nothing inside wooldid needs it.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming cleanmatrices stops with r(198). The fix is to replace it with `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` before the call. Retire test_adopath.do (or keep only A0 as an adopath smoke test), test_stored S9, test_s6 S5, the ext config, and the isolation branch in mkrun.py. The cap-wrapped kernel calls could then become honest errors.

candidates.what_it_is: Under subgroups(), skips the per-subgroup estimates and reports only the pairwise contrasts and the equality test, pitched as a speed option.
candidates.why_delete: The speed gain is mostly gone. EFF3 already reads the subgroup level margins out of the same pwcompare pass that makes the contrasts (ado 3398-3404, 3713-3720), so the main and pre-treatment level rows cost nothing extra. The option now saves only the per-subgroup event-study passes (4380), the per-subgroup ame level passes (3868), the per-subgroup escomp pass (4695) and the per-subgroup joint tests (5131); on a run with no event-study window and no contreat() it saves essentially nothing. It still needs a parallel plumbing path.
candidates.burden_evidence: 35 ado references and 11 branches. A dedicated hidden result e(wdid_sglev), built in three places (3725, 3823, 4159/4222), exists only so the degeneracy guard can see level rows when the tables are suppressed. It is refused by both engines (permctl 6673, bootctl 7407). There are replay branches (12780, 13007, 14986, 15147) and 3 display cautions and 3 adversarial skip cautions keyed on it (guide ch.14 rows 949-951, 1064-1066). It caused a high-severity defect, 'sgdeg-inert-under-suppresssg': the BS-15 degenerate-contrast guard was silently inert under it (changes_review_2026-09-22:52/108, fixed 637062e). Tests: test_sgdegen.do, test_permute3.do, test_bootstrap_gates.do, 1 ext config, degeneracy_scan.py.
candidates.value_evidence: The contrasts and the joint equality test, which are its whole output, come from the default run anyway. The per-subgroup rows it hides are simply extra output the user can ignore. The only real saving is the per-subgroup event-study cost, and a user can get that by dropping the event-study window for the contrast run.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198). The same call without it returns a superset of the results, a little slower when an event-study window is requested. Retire its legs in test_sgdegen, test_permute3 and test_bootstrap_gates, 1 config row, and the e(wdid_sglev) branch in degeneracy_scan.py.

candidates.what_it_is: A bias-corrected and accelerated interval and p-value family, whose acceleration comes from a delete-one-cluster jackknife of G extra fits.
candidates.why_delete: It is the largest single display family: about 300 lines, an extra estimation loop and its own refusal and caution. The author has already judged it not worth completing: the 07 Sep ruling declined the per-cell jackknife, so the gteffects and cfx cells silently fall back to the bc family under it. The external route is Stata's own prefix, which the help already endorses.
candidates.burden_evidence: 124 bca/jkacc/jackknife references. The jackknife loop in bootrun (ado 10786-10820, with its own dots line and runtime projection). Mata wooldid_bootbca (54 lines) and wooldid_bootppa (51 lines). BCa twin matrices for coefficients (wmbca, bootwire 11080-11158) and for pairwise contrasts (pwbca, bootjnt 8231-8495) with their own missing-family counters and caution. The bca-to-bc remap and its caution for gteffects and cfx cells (7608-7613). A refusal without cluster() (7256) and a refusal with boottstat (7356). Hidden e(boot_bca_pwsgs), e(boot_accel), e(boot_ci_bca) and e(boot_p_bca). Two separate rulings about its p-floor line (changes_review 09-22 rows 'p-floor line under bootdisplay(bca)'). Tests: battery config boot_bca_c2 (baseline boot_bca_c2.csv), test_bootstrap_joint, test_bootstrap_df, test_bootstrap_gates, test_bootstrap_tstat, and the stdbca arm of mc_bootse2.
candidates.value_evidence: Percentile (the default) and bc cover the asymmetric-interval use. The one Monte-Carlo design run (mc/out2/bootstrap/tables.md, cfg BA, n=15) shows no gain over percentile (BCa 86.7% vs percentile 93.3%, MCSE about 8.8, so this is noise, not miscalibration). Users who want BCa can run `bootstrap _b, bca reps(#) cluster(c): wooldid ...` without weights, which the help documents as supported.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file with bootdisplay(bca) stops with r(198); bc is the closest in-package substitute. Retire battery config boot_bca_c2 and its baseline CSV, the bca legs in 4 cert files, and the stdbca MC arm. No other family's numbers move.

candidates.what_it_is: Adjusts the bias-correction constant z0 by half-counting replications that exactly equal the observed statistic, as Stata's bootstrap ties option does.
candidates.why_delete: The help says so itself: 'It has no effect on continuous statistics.' Every statistic wooldid bootstraps is continuous, so the option is a no-op except on exact numeric ties, which are essentially only degenerate draws. It is still threaded through the whole bootstrap kernel.
candidates.burden_evidence: A flag passed through 8 call sites (ado 564, 587, 635, 5776, 7658-7706 cell wires, 8315, 8344, 8375, 11011, 11022, 11039) and taken as a parameter by 6 Mata functions (wooldid_bootcellwire, bootpp, bootppa, bootci, bootbca, boottp; the z0 lines at 17095, 17611, 17729, 17824, 17879). It is also forwarded in the replication 'stray' list (7160) and posted as e(boot_ties). Battery config boot_bayes_sgjt carries it ('the ties z0 convention'), along with test_bootstrap_joint and configs.csv.
candidates.value_evidence: No wooldid statistic has a discrete sampling distribution. The only counterweight is naming symmetry with Stata's bootstrap prefix. An alternative to deleting outright is to apply the half-count always, which changes no number on continuous statistics, and drop the switch.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming ties stops with r(198). Numerically nothing moves on continuous statistics. The boot_bayes_sgjt battery config needs 'ties' dropped from its command line (and a re-bless only if a tie ever occurred there), plus its leg in test_bootstrap_joint.

candidates.what_it_is: Skips the standard errors of the continuous-treatment plot cells to save time.
candidates.why_delete: This speed knob already has a global counterpart in fastnose, and its interaction with the two engines has produced a run of defects and new cautions. Under both engines the cells now keep replication inference anyway, so it does nothing there, and it is dropped under permtstat and boottstat.
candidates.burden_evidence: 27 ado references. Three defects and rulings in the 09-22 round alone: 'permtstat-cfxplotnose-blank' (high: every cfx cell's inference blank with no message; a new caution was approved), 'D5 cfxplotnose-engine-asymmetry' (permute kept the 6-column shape while bootstrap truncated it; built 516038c), and 'D5 follow-up: boottstat with cfxplotnose' (another override caution). The help entry is now mostly a list of where it is dropped. Tests: test_bootstrap_df, test_fastnose, test_permute3, battery config perm_cfxnose (baseline perm_cfxnose.csv), 2 config rows.
candidates.value_evidence: The saving is the variance part of the cfx plot margins on analytic runs only. fastnose gives a bigger saving for exploratory runs, and the final run needs the SEs anyway. Under bootstrap() and permute() it already has no effect.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198). Analytic runs with makecfxplots become slower, and their plots gain confidence bands. Retire battery config perm_cfxnose and its legs in 3 cert files.

candidates.what_it_is: Reports the plain absolute-value permutation share c/n with no add-one adjustment, the number ritest and Stata's permute prefix print.
candidates.why_delete: It duplicates permabsp. Under permexact the two are identical (both use ma/n when the reference set contains the observed draw), and they use the same intervals. For sampled draws the raw number is recoverable exactly: p_raw = ((n+1)*p_absp - 1)/n. Deleting it also shrinks the mutually exclusive triple permabsp/permside()/permrawp that the blue-sky review flagged as confusing (structure_and_ux.md:760; never ruled).
candidates.burden_evidence: 19 ado references. Convention code 2, set in 4 places (6736, 9007, 9391, 9841) and threaded to Mata permtail (the absp==2 branch). An exclusion error (6639-6640). Its own footer text and zero-print rules (12216, 13166), and e(perm_pconv)='raw'. Tests: test_permute3.do, 1 config row, degeneracy_scan.py, and the suite's external oracle legs newfeat/ritest_crosscheck.do, mc_ri2.do and analyze_mcri2.py, which are written against it.
candidates.value_evidence: It exists for cross-checking against ritest. The add-one form (the default family and permabsp) is the valid p-value for sampled draws, and the raw share can print an exact 0, which the help itself has to explain.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming permrawp stops with r(198). ritest_crosscheck.do and the mc_ri2 raw arm must compute the raw share from permabsp with the formula above. 1 config and the test_permute3 legs retire.

candidates.what_it_is: An alternative adversarial pre-trend test that fits the trend line on the pre-period coefficients only and tests whether the post-period coefficients follow the projected line.
candidates.why_delete: It is a second implementation of a diagnostic whose primary version already carries many caveats, and it has no calibration edge. In the stored MC (mc/out/advb_report.md AB11, AB17-AB21) it passes where the primary passes (AB11 4.4% at nominal 5%) and fails in the same regimes: containment 37.7%, cohort shock 36.7%, G=5 11.3%, and robust AR(1) inert at 0.6%. Each engine must carry both.
candidates.burden_evidence: 18 ado references. The alt flag runs through wooldid_advstat and its gap backstop (14382-14446), Mata wooldid_advW and advx, the bootstrap statistic columns '_a1' (10360) and bootadvobs (17180-17266), and the permute permadv and permadvline paths (9637-9686, 18421-18673). A standalone error (6282) and a cancelled-test caution (1234). Tests: test_advstat, test_advguard, test_ptpdisp, battery configs adv_altb and adv_r2001 (baselines adv_altb.csv, adv_r2001.csv), 6 config rows, mc_adv.do and mc_advb.do.
candidates.value_evidence: It tests a genuinely different null (post coefficients against the pre-trend forecast). But the pretrendpower() slope and bias columns and honestdid on e(b_es_*)/e(V_es_*) cover the forecast-style question, and do it better. No calibration advantage was measured.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file with it stops with r(198). The primary adversarial test is unchanged. Retire battery configs adv_altb and adv_r2001 (or re-point them at the primary), their baselines, 6 config rows, and the altmethod arms of test_advstat, test_advguard, test_ptpdisp and the mc_adv drivers.

candidates.what_it_is: Draws a frequency histogram of cohort-level effects (and, under contreat(), ame_i) and posts the underlying vector as e(histogramestimates).
candidates.why_delete: For binary treatments e(gteffects) supersedes it: gteffects posts every cohort-by-period effect with its weights and exactly reproduces any per-cohort aggregate. The histogram's own matrix is weak output: its row names are volatile wooldid tempvar names (ado ~14004-14008 says so), so the user cannot tell which cohort a row belongs to, despite the help's 'for the user to manipulate'.
candidates.burden_evidence: The self-contained program wooldid_hist is about 130 lines (13949-14080), with 4 extra margins passes and 4 graphs. The engines must each state that it is untouched by replication, in the help and in comments (684-690). A blue-sky finding showed its caution under permute contradicting the footer (structure_and_ux.md:688). Tests: test_fastcollapse, test_stored (S10), test_poismargins, 7 config rows, degeneracy_scan.py.
candidates.value_evidence: For binary treatments, gteffects plus one line of collapse and histogram in the user's own code gives the same picture, with cohort keys. The one thing lost is the ame_i histogram under contreat(), where gteffects is refused, so that case has no in-package substitute.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198). Users on contreat() lose the ame_i distribution. Retire 7 config rows and the legs in 3 cert files.

candidates.what_it_is: Builds the lattice() quantiles without the sample weights.
candidates.why_delete: This small knob has an obvious do-it-yourself route, and it has just cost a bootstrap fix that left a process-global switch behind. It has no entry of its own in the help (only one mention).
candidates.burden_evidence: 9 ado references. The weight-inserter logic at 1292-1296. The WOOLDID_REPLATW global, carried through the replication harness so replications re-bin on the resample (ruled 'Fix it' 09-23, built a977d58, global cleared bfbaa81; see ado 22 and 10704). Forwarded in both engines' replication option strings (221, 440). Tests: test_bootstrap_std.do, 1 ext config, degeneracy_scan.py.
candidates.value_evidence: A user can run `gquantiles lat = dose, xtile nquantiles(#) by(...)` without weights and pass lattice(lat). The caveat is that a precomputed lattice is fixed across bootstrap replications rather than re-formed on each resample, which is exactly the behaviour a977d58 built. That is a real but second-order difference.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198). Users switch to a precomputed unweighted lattice variable, whose bins do not re-form per bootstrap replication. Retire its leg in test_bootstrap_std and 1 config.

considered_and_kept: permtci: the author ruled 'Keep it' on 2026-09-23 (changes_review_2026-09-22.md:277), although permtstat+permabsp gives the same interval (checked in Mata permtail: b ± q(|t|)*se).
anticipation and gteffects: proposed for removal before and kept by the author's ruling of 2026-08-19.

ccc_absorb(): heavy interaction burden (poisson retry paths, collapse eligibility, bootstrap re-id, the 3201 split fix), but the 09-07 and 09-23 rulings chose to maintain it, and it is the memory route for coarse cohort controls.

impvalues: carries the largest burden numbers of any non-engine option (78 references, about 12 refusals and message rows, and it changes the estimand), but it is a headline inference method with no in-package substitute, and the author is actively maintaining it (R-A ruling 09-22).

customvce(): a large refusal list, but it is the only route to HC2/HC3 and regress's vce() family (for example CR2-type small-cluster corrections); the regress path it uses is shared with unconditionalse anyway.
emptycellsoverride: value near zero, but the burden is trivial (6 references) and it is the escape hatch for a global Stata setting wooldid changes.
esrelativeto(): an event-study option (outside this lens); merging it into esfixedbaseperiod(#) would be a rename, not a deletion.
permside(): one-sided p-values are a legitimate inferential choice with no other route; cheap once the convention code exists.
permanalyticse: restores e(V) and the analytic column under permute, which honestdid and pretrends handoffs need.
bootdf(): moderate burden, but it keeps e(df_r) consistent with the Wald family and the test/lincom path; at most the integer-df form could go.
permstepdown, permstrata, permprobs, permexact, permonsetcohorts: core design features of the randomization engine, well tested against external oracles.
bootsave()/permsave(): the only way to inspect replication draws beyond 10,000 and to audit the engines.
boottstat: large, but it is the only route to bootstrapped adversarial and studentized contrasts.
simultaneousbands, pretrendpower(), jointtests, adversarial: event-study inference (outside this lens).
makecfxplotsbysg, cfxlattice(), cfxplottypes(): small, self-contained continuous-treatment plot knobs, cheap relative to what they give.
ccnoabsorb: a stability lever on the ppmlhdfe and continuous-control paths that the 09-23 poisson work leans on (the poly-explicit spelling reuses it).
customweightmultiplier(): moderate burden, but it is the only route to bespoke estimands with inference; gteffects aggregation gives points without a covariance.
summarystats, verbose, regtol(), update, dots(), rseed(), level(), saveplots(), replace, makeplots: cheap, with ordinary expected functions.
the twelve lattice types: about 30 lines of dispatch in total; pruning them would save little.

deletion_lenses.lens: Redundancy and overlap: options that duplicate another option, an external tool or a Stata command; aliases and deprecated spellings; knobs whose default is the only sensible setting; outputs whose information another output already carries. Scope was the sthlp syntax table and every option entry (lines 60-930), the stored-results section (969-1110), guide chapters 10-11 and 13, and, for each candidate, the ado (branches, refusals, messages), the suite configs (configs.csv, configs_ext.csv) and the cert do-files under test/. Candidates were checked against the author's rulings in review_process (changes_review_2026-09-22, rulings_2026-09-07, option_consolidation_2026-09-16 and the QR rulings of 2026-09-06). The option_consolidation ruling set the precedent: a clean break with no alias. oldsyntax is ignored because another agent is removing it. Working notes: /var/folders/ls/yldcbdg94wq_f401f_nynbsc0000gn/T/wooldid_e098/review/notes/delete_redundancy.md

candidates.what_it_is: A speed toggle under subgroups() that skips the per-subgroup effect tables and reports only the pairwise subgroup contrasts and the equality test.
candidates.why_delete: Its only documented value is speed, and most of that speed is already free. The EFF3 comment at ado 3393-3400 and the grab at ado 3710-3720 show that the pwcompare(effects) pass producing the contrasts already returns the subgroup level margins in r(table), and wooldid reads them from there. So the option saves only the by-subgroup event-study and pre-period passes (ado 4380 on). fastnose and a narrower window are the general speed levers. The option also has its own hidden plumbing (e(wdid_suppresssgpe), and e(wdid_sglev) added in 637062e) that exists only so the degenerate-contrast guard keeps working under it.
candidates.burden_evidence: About 20 branches in ado keyed on the option: worker 3393, 3683-3730, 3821, 3868, 4157, 4220, 4380, 4695, 4787, 5131, 5178-5186; hidden macro at 5265; replay 12599, 12780, 13007, 14986, 15147. Two refusals: 'permute() may not be combined with suppresssgprimaryeffects' (6674) and the bootstrap twin (7411), plus an impossible-state guard at 10967. It already caused one high-severity defect, sgdeg-inert-under-suppresssg: the degenerate-contrast guard was silently inert under the option (changes_review:52/108/137, built 637062e). Tests: ext_cov10_suppress_sg, test_sgdegen.do, test_bootstrap_gates.do and test_permute3.do refusal legs, 137 lines across 9 do-files. Help: an option entry plus refusal lists in the bootstrap() and permute() entries. Guide: 14 mentions.
candidates.value_evidence: A user who wants only the contrasts can ignore the subgroup tables. The post-treatment subgroup levels come from the same margins call anyway. The only real saving is the per-subgroup event-study passes on runs with a window and many subgroups, and fastnose or a narrower window covers that during specification search. Neither replication engine accepts the option.
candidates.what_breaks: Do-files that pass suppresssgprimaryeffects stop with r(198). A run without it prints and posts the per-subgroup tables (e(wdidsgresults_*)) and runs slower on wide event-study windows with many subgroups. Point estimates and contrasts do not change.

candidates.what_it_is: A technical option that runs `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` at the start and end of a run to recover a session that reghdfe has left in a bad state.
candidates.why_delete: It is exactly two Stata commands that any user can type (`clear mata` and `matrix drop _all`). It is also destructive: `matrix drop _all` deletes all of the user's own matrices, which the help does not say. And it drops wooldid's own Mata kernels partway through the run, which has forced defensive design elsewhere in the code.
candidates.burden_evidence: ado 797-801 and 5350-5353. The inline Mata anchor at ado 14763-14768 exists only because a named helper would be cleared. The cap-wrapped Mata calls at ado 12371 and 12524-12530 exist for the same reason: under a `do`-loaded build the kernels do not come back, so e(V) silently falls back from analytic-blocks to analytic-diagonal. Two cert harnesses cover this side effect: test_adopath.do legs A1-A3 (change audit 2026-09-22, cleanmatrices-cert-gap) and test_stored.do S9, which pins completion under the degraded state. There is also one ext config (ext_bin_ext_cleanmatrices). 86 lines across 10 test do-files.
candidates.value_evidence: The help frames it as recovering from occasional reghdfe crashes. The user can run `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` (or `discard`) before rerunning and get the same recovery without wooldid deleting matrices mid-run. The 2026-09-22 audit found that it runs cleanly but adds nothing an estimate depends on.
candidates.what_breaks: Do-files that pass cleanmatrices stop with r(198) and need `clear mata` / `matrix drop _all` typed before the call. No estimate changes. A do-loaded harness run keeps analytic-blocks e(V) where cleanmatrices used to drop it to analytic-diagonal.

candidates.what_it_is: A technical option that skips wooldid's `set emptycells drop`, which roughly doubles runtime and gives the same results.
candidates.why_delete: The default is the only sensible setting. The help says the override 'should only be of interest in conjunction with verbose' and the guide's lever 7 says it is 'rarely wanted'. The 2026-09-22 audit confirmed that 'emptycellsoverride and ccnoabsorb agree with their controls' (changes_review:249). A user who wants the raw regression with empty cells can re-run the verbose-printed command after `set emptycells keep`.
candidates.burden_evidence: Small code (ado 806-812, forwarded into replication command lines at ado 221 and 440, in both syntax lines and the wdv_ret list at 6322), but it carries a full help entry, a sentence in the Runtime section, a guide lever and a guide mention. One test config (ext_cov10_technical_options). It adds an axis to every replication forwarding list.
candidates.value_evidence: It changes no estimate. The verbose option already prints the regression command, so inspecting the model with empty cells kept takes one `set emptycells keep` and a re-run of that command outside wooldid.
candidates.what_breaks: Do-files that pass the option stop with r(198). Nothing else changes.

candidates.what_it_is: The bootstrap(bayes) variant that gives each cluster a Gamma shape equal to its row count and spreads the drawn mass over its rows, matching bayesboot's id() convention.
candidates.why_delete: It exists only to reproduce another tool. The help's own words are that it 'is for comparison against that command only; on panel data it understates the standard errors badly'. A variant the documentation calls wrong for the package's main use case is burden with negative value. Without it, bootalpha() has one legal value and the option can go too.
candidates.burden_evidence: 28 ado lines: validation and two errors (7237-7250, 'bootalpha() must be either...' and 'bootalpha() applies only to bootstrap(bayes)'), the Mata shape and row-spread branch (16184-16207), bootsave's per-cluster weight rescaling (600), defaults in bootrun and bootwire (10005, 10908) and e(boot_alpha) (11643). The bootsave() help sentence carries a 'divided by the cluster's observation count under bootalpha(size)' clause. Tests: two configs run it, boot_bayes in the core battery (configs.csv:120) and real_boot_alpha (configs.csv:224), so the core battery pins the variant the help calls harmful. Also test_bootstrap_bayes.do, test_bootstrap_gates.do and mc/mc_bootse.do (47 lines across the do-files).
candidates.value_evidence: No applied user needs bayesboot's convention inside wooldid. bootalpha(equal), the default Rubin convention, is the one F058's coverage study measured (research_2026-09-06/F058_bootstrap.md s3). A cross-check against bayesboot can be run outside wooldid, since bootsave() writes the Dirichlet weights.
candidates.what_breaks: bootalpha(size) runs stop with r(198). boot_bayes and real_boot_alpha must be re-pointed to the default and the battery re-blessed, since their bootstrap SEs move. The bayes test legs and mc_bootse.do lose their size arm. bootstrap(bayes) itself is unaffected.

candidates.what_it_is: `wooldid, update` runs `net install wooldid, from(<github raw URL>) replace` and exits.
candidates.why_delete: It is a five-line wrapper around a standard Stata command that users of any net-installed package already know (`net install ... replace`, or `adoupdate` for a matching source). It occupies a syntax-table slot and a help entry, and it has already caused a defect: shell-update-stale-cfxsave, where `wooldid, update` re-ran the analytic plot-data write on the previous run's e() (fixed e203b93, changes_review:140).
candidates.burden_evidence: ado 756-760. The shell and replay paths had to be taught not to act on stale e() under it (e203b93). A help entry and a guide line. No suite config, so the path is untested apart from the defect fix.
candidates.value_evidence: One-word convenience for a package distributed only through GitHub. The same result comes from `net install wooldid, from("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thegland/wooldid/main/wooldidinstall/") replace`, which the help could print instead.
candidates.what_breaks: Users who type `wooldid, update` get r(198) and must use net install. The help's install section would need the URL spelled out.

candidates.what_it_is: A permute() p-value convention that reports the plain absolute-value share c/n without the add-one adjustment, the number ritest reports.
candidates.why_delete: It is permabsp without the +1. Under permexact the two are identical (both ma/n, ado permtail ~18040). On sampled draws the raw share follows from what permabsp already posts: raw = ((n+1)*p_abs - 1)/n with n = e(perm_n). It adds one more convention to a mutually exclusive set of three options, a sixth branch to every permutation kernel, and the only route by which a sampled permutation p can print exactly 0, which the display then has to explain. Note: the author named this option and ruled it in on 2026-09-06 (F052, 'reproduces ritest's number'), so deleting it reverses a three-week-old ruling.
candidates.burden_evidence: 19 ado lines. The convention code is threaded through permctl (6639-6640 mutual-exclusion error, 6722-6738 floor caution), permwire (9002-9007), permjnt (9388-9391), permcellsx (9838-9841), the Mata permtail (17991-18050) and a dedicated footer sentence (13166), plus the add-one-free exception in the p = 0 resolution logic (12216). Test legs: the config perm_rawp, test_permute3.do and the permute cert files (153 lines across 13 do-files). The external-benchmark ritest oracle keys on it.
candidates.value_evidence: It serves a user who wants wooldid's p to match ritest digit for digit. permabsp gives the principled absolute-value p, which is valid on sampled draws where the raw share is anti-conservative, and the raw figure is one arithmetic step from permabsp plus e(perm_n).
candidates.what_breaks: permrawp runs stop with r(198). The perm_rawp config and the ritest cross-check need re-pointing to permabsp plus the conversion. e(perm_pconv) loses the value 'raw'.

candidates.what_it_is: A permute() option that replaces the displayed two-sided p-values with the one-sided left or right share.
candidates.why_delete: The information is already posted on every permute() run. e(perm_p_lo) and e(perm_p_hi) are posted unconditionally (ado 9220-9227, kernel rows 14-15), aligned by name to e(b), and the pairwise contrasts' kernel (the hidden e(perm_pwsgs_kernel), 18 rows) carries the same one-sided rows. So the option mostly chooses which already-computed number goes into the p column and e(p). It also leaves the intervals two-sided, so p and interval disagree under it, which the help has to explain.
candidates.burden_evidence: 19 ado lines: the syntax check and error (6635-6636), the three-way mutual-exclusion error (6639-6640), convention codes 3 and 4 threaded through permwire, permjnt, permcellsx and Mata permtail, a floor-caution branch, and a dedicated footer sentence (13170). Tests: the config perm_side_left and 111 lines across 19 do-files.
candidates.value_evidence: A user with a one-sided hypothesis reads e(perm_p_lo) or e(perm_p_hi) by coefficient name. What would be lost is the one-sided p of the continuous-treatment plot cells, which permcellsx forms under the option but which is not posted separately by default.
candidates.what_breaks: permside() runs stop with r(198). Users read e(perm_p_lo)/e(perm_p_hi) instead of the printed column. The perm_side_left config is re-pointed. The one-sided p of the cfx plot cells is no longer available.

candidates.feature: Deprecated and legacy stored-result aliases: e(perm_lb_est)/e(perm_ub_est), e(permdist), e(boot_percentile_mainresults) (and, optionally, the legacy per-estimand scalars e(perm_p_est)/e(perm_sd_est))
candidates.what_it_is: Duplicate e() names kept after renames: the lb/ub scalars duplicate e(perm_bandlo_est)/e(perm_bandhi_est); e(permdist) is superseded by e(permdist_b) and has a misleading name; e(boot_percentile_mainresults) aliases e(boot_pctl_mainresults); and the per-estimand p/sd scalars repeat entries of e(perm_p) and e(perm_sd).
candidates.why_delete: These are pure aliases, and the help itself calls the first two deprecated, noting that lb/ub means a genuine interval bound elsewhere in wooldid, which the null band is not. The author ruled on 2026-09-07 (CS-57/58, CS-54) to keep them with a documented deprecation. The oldsyntax removal shows he is now willing to cut compatibility surface, and these are the next items of that kind.
candidates.burden_evidence: ado 306-342 (the scalar and matrix postings, including the 10,000-rep cap on e(permdist)), the draw-cap caution at 415 that names e(permdist), the dense legacy permdist packing at ~8953, and the replay display at ado 13235, which still reads the deprecated e(perm_lb_)/e(perm_ub_). Help: a paragraph of alias notes in the stored-results section. Guide ch.13 carries long explanations of why e(permdist) is not the twin of e(bootdist). Tests: e(perm_lb_) appears in 9 do-files, e(permdist) in 8, and perm_*.csv baselines pin them.
candidates.value_evidence: Every number is posted under its correct name. Only do-files written before the 2026-09-07 renames read the old names.
candidates.what_breaks: Old do-files that read e(perm_lb_att) or e(permdist) get missing values. Replay must be switched to e(perm_bandlo_/bandhi_) (ado 13235). test_permute*.do, test_stored.do and the perm baselines drop those columns, so a battery re-bless follows.

candidates.what_it_is: A bootstrap() option that adjusts the bias-corrected median-bias constant z0 for replications exactly equal to the observed statistic, mirroring the ties option of Stata's bootstrap.
candidates.why_delete: The help says it 'has no effect on continuous statistics', and every wooldid bootstrap statistic is continuous. An exact tie occurs only when a pairs resample reproduces the original cluster multiset bit for bit, which is rare except with very few clusters. That is the regime where wooldid already cautions (fewer than 6 treated clusters) and points users to permute().
candidates.burden_evidence: Threaded as a flag through about 15 call sites: bootctl (7160), bootwire (564, 10895, 11005-11039, e(boot_ties) at 11531), bootjnt (587, 8315, 8344, 8375), bootcellsx (635, 7658-7706), and Mata bootci/bootbca/boottp/bootpp/bootcellwire. One config (boot_aw_ties) and legs in the bootstrap cert files.
candidates.value_evidence: No wooldid design in the suite has shown it moving a number. Stata's prefix supports it for discrete statistics, and wooldid computes none.
candidates.what_breaks: boot_aw_ties and do-files that pass ties stop with r(198). e(boot_ties) is no longer posted. No reported number changes except in the rare exact-tie case at very few clusters.

candidates.feature: ccc_absorb() (with ccnoabsorb as the same class)
candidates.what_it_is: An alternate spelling of coarsecohortcontrols(c.x) that puts the cell-by-control interactions i._i#i._t#c.(x) in absorb() rather than the regressor list, paired with ccnoabsorb, which moves continuous-treatment controls out of absorb().
candidates.why_delete: Both are absorb-versus-explicit choices for the same estimand. ccc_absorb builds the same terms as coarsecohortcontrols (ado 1396-1401, and guide ch.10's table says 'as coarsecohortcontrols(), continuous variables only, absorbed'), and the 2026-09-22 audit found ccnoabsorb agrees with its control (changes_review:249). The burden sits in the ppmlhdfe interplay: an r(3200) retry, an r(3201) split of 2+ variables per term, and a reversal on the plain-basic poisson path.
candidates.burden_evidence: 31 ado lines for ccc_absorb: an absorb inserter, a ppmlhdfe split loop (1601-1640), the r(3200) fallback message (1941), cautions on the regress path (5452), collapse-eligibility detection (5885-5929), bootstrap re-identification substitution (458) and replication forwarding (227). The help paragraph on poisson has three clauses about it. Three rulings in two days (changes_review:287-288, including a reversal on 2026-09-24). ccnoabsorb adds 12 ado lines. Tests: a few configs each.
candidates.value_evidence: The help credits ccc_absorb with memory efficiency and ccnoabsorb with estimation stability. The poisson saga of 2026-09-23/24 shows the stability concern is real, and the author's recent rulings suggest he values the absorbed route. Listed for completeness only.
candidates.what_breaks: Memory-bound runs with many continuous coarse controls would have to use coarsecohortcontrols(c.x) as explicit regressors. ccnoabsorb users would lose the manual stability lever. Poisson paths that already enter these terms explicitly would not change.

considered_and_kept: permtci: the author ruled KEEP on 2026-09-23 (changes_review:277, 'permtci redundant with permtstat permabsp')

altmethod_adversarial: not redundant. Its null (post coefficients on the line extrapolated from the pre-period) is nested in, not the same as, adversarial's (all coefficients on one line). It is the standard extrapolate-the-pretrend test, and its covariance was fixed on 2026-09-13
latticeignoreweights: a real choice (unweighted bins under sampling weights), and the author just paid to fix it under bootstrap (a977d58)
permanalyticse: its refusal with fastnose was just ruled and built (8443694), and it is the only way to get analytic SEs beside permutation p's without studentizing
cfxplotnose: a partial fastnose. The plot-cell SEs are the expensive margins calls, and fastnose would drop the main SEs too, so it has a use nothing else covers
makecfxplotsbysg: a runtime and plot-count toggle, which is reasonable because per-subgroup cfx plots multiply the number of graphs
customvce(): the only route to HC2/HC3, jackknife and other vce() forms that reghdfe does not offer
bootstrap(bayes) as a mode: excluded by the brief (engine modes), and it has a distinct property (no cluster leaves the sample). Only its bootalpha(size) variant is proposed
bootdf() and bootdisplay() families: separate display/reference-distribution axes. bootdf(normal) maps to Stata's bootstrap prefix convention, which the external benchmark relies on
permabsp: the principled absolute-value convention, kept as the survivor if permrawp goes
permstepdown vs simultaneousbands: engine-specific multiplicity tools (each refused with the other engine), not overlapping

pretrendpower(): overlaps Roth's pretrends package on the mdt_nis column (cross-checked to 2.5e-4), but mdt_wald, the GLS slope and the implied bias have no counterpart there, and it follows the bootstrap covariance
histogramcohorteffects: overlaps gteffects for a binary treatment (cohort effects are weighted means of cells), but it is the only cohort-level view under contreat(), where gteffects is refused
summarystats: the only console display of the e(escomp) composition table
gteffects: the cell-level surface that makes custom aggregations reproducible
esrelativeto(): a real knob. Letting it imply esfixedbaseperiod would remove a no-op caution, but that is a consolidation, not a deletion
regtol(), verbose, dots(), rseed(), bootsave()/permsave(), replace: each has a distinct, commonly needed job
robust, unconditionalse, impvalues, level(): distinct inference choices

coarsecohortcontrols(), interactivecontrols(), timetrends, fe(), controls(): distinct model terms (interactivecontrols reports the variation as part of the effects, while coarsecohortcontrols partials it out)
customweightmultiplier(): the only route to bespoke margins weights
contreatelasticitytype(dyex): a distinct estimand (elasticity vs unit effect). Only the help's sentence about the removed eyex/eydx forms is residue

candidates.what_it_is: Runs `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` at the start and end of the call, as a recovery for sessions that reghdfe has left in a bad Mata state.
candidates.why_delete: The same recovery is two commands the user can type before the call, choosing what to lose, while the option also clears wooldid's own Mata kernels mid-run. That forced an inline-Mata screen (ado ~14763), cap-wrapped kernel calls that quietly drop e(V) to the analytic diagonal under a do-loaded build (12371, 12524), a whole cert file (test_adopath.do) and a dedicated shard-isolation branch in test/suite/mkrun.py:261-271.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming cleanmatrices stops with r(198) and should type `clear mata` and `matrix drop _all` before the call instead; no estimate changes (a one-sentence recovery note could stay in Bugs and Assistance).

candidates.feature: bootalpha() (the size convention, and with it the whole option)
candidates.what_it_is: Chooses the bootstrap(bayes) Dirichlet convention: equal (the default, Rubin's cluster Bayesian bootstrap) or size (Gamma shape equal to cluster row count, matching bayesboot with id()).
candidates.why_delete: The help's own entry says size is 'for comparison against that command only; on panel data it understates the standard errors badly', so its only non-default value is wrong on the package's core data type and has produced three recorded defects (bb-02, HV-BOOT-02, the 09-22 w_ column help fix). With size gone the option has one value and goes too; bayesboot itself remains the route for that convention.
candidates.what_breaks: bootstrap(bayes) runs are unchanged, but a do-file naming bootalpha() stops with r(198), e(boot_alpha) is no longer posted, and the core config boot_bayes and real_boot_alpha (both run size) must be re-pointed to the default and re-blessed.

candidates.what_it_is: Under subgroups(), skips the per-subgroup estimates and reports only the pairwise subgroup contrasts and the equality test, as a speed option.
candidates.why_delete: Since EFF3 the subgroup level margins come free from the pwcompare pass that makes the contrasts (ado 3393-3404, 3710-3720), so it now saves only the per-subgroup event-study, AME and escomp passes (measured 11.8 s to 6.6 s on a windowed run, identical e(pwsgs)). It still forks the worker into about 20 branches with its own hidden e(wdid_sglev) path, is refused by both engines, and hid the high-severity sgdeg-inert-under-suppresssg defect (built 637062e).
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198); the same call without it returns a superset of the results, roughly 1.8x slower on subgroup runs with an event-study window.

candidates.what_it_is: Half-counts bootstrap replications exactly equal to the rep-0 comparator when forming the bias-correction constant z0, as the ties option of Stata's bootstrap does.
candidates.why_delete: The help already says it has no effect on continuous statistics, and a probe at G=5 (dta_binary, cluster = mod(i,5), reps 300) showed it is inert even in the one regime where ties should occur: the 8 identity draws land 1 ulp (4.4e-16) from the comparator, never bitwise equal, and e(boot_z0) and e(boot_ci_bc) are bit-identical with and without ties. It is still threaded as a flag through about 15 call sites and six Mata functions.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming ties stops with r(198) and e(boot_ties) is no longer posted; no reported number moves (the battery config boot_bayes_sgjt drops the word from its command line).

candidates.what_it_is: Makes the printed permutation p-values one-sided (share at or below, or at or above, the observed statistic).
candidates.why_delete: Every permute() run already posts both one-sided shares unconditionally, by coefficient name, as e(perm_p_lo) and e(perm_p_hi) (ado 9221-9227; the footer says so), and the interval stays two-sided under the option anyway, so it mainly chooses which stored number fills the p column at the cost of convention codes 3/4 in four programs. The burden lens kept it as a legitimate inferential choice; the alternative short of deletion is the blue-sky merge of permabsp/permside()/permrawp into one permp() option (structure_and_ux.md, never ruled).
candidates.what_breaks: The printed p column, e(p) and so esttab can no longer carry a one-sided p (users read e(perm_p_lo)/e(perm_p_hi)), and the continuous-treatment plot cells lose their one-sided variant, rebuildable only from permsave().

candidates.what_it_is: Reports the plain absolute-value permutation share c/n without the add-one adjustment, the number ritest and Stata's permute prefix print.
candidates.why_delete: It is permabsp without the +1: identical under permexact, and on sampled draws recoverable exactly as ((n+1)*p_absp - 1)/n with n from e(perm_n), while being the anti-conservative form and the only route by which a sampled permutation p prints exactly 0. Deleting it reverses your 2026-09-06 ruling (F052), which named and admitted it to reproduce ritest's number.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming permrawp stops with r(198), and the ritest cross-check (newfeat/ritest_crosscheck.do), the mc_ri2 raw arm and the perm_rawp config must convert from permabsp by hand.

candidates.what_it_is: Under permute(), takes the observed run out of fast mode so the analytic standard errors fill the se_analytic column and e(V), e(b_es_*) and e(V_es_*) are posted.
candidates.why_delete: Only the observed run leaves fast mode (ado 6195, 6243), so every number it adds is exactly what the plain analytic run of the same specification gives, at the cost of one base fit, and permtstat already shows the analytic SEs. It has carried three defects in the 09-22 review plus a permute+contreat+subgroups+ES abort; the burden and redundancy lenses both kept it as the one-call route to analytic SEs beside permutation p's for the honestdid handoff.
candidates.what_breaks: Under default permute() the se_analytic column stays blank and no e(V)/e(V_es_*) is posted, so a user wanting both, or feeding honestdid, runs the analytic specification separately.

candidates.what_it_is: A modifier of adversarial that fits a line to the pre-period coefficients plus the reference and tests the post coefficients jointly against its forward projection.
candidates.why_delete: It is a second statistic for an already niche diagnostic, threaded through every engine (a gapskip status all four call sites branch on, a separate Mata forecast branch, the permute and bootstrap statistic columns), and the stored MC shows no calibration edge over the primary test; honestdid's smoothness restriction with M = 0 on e(b_es_*)/e(V_es_*) answers the forecast question as an interval. The redundancy lens dissented: its null (post coefficients on the extrapolated pre-trend) is nested in, not the same as, adversarial's, and it is the standard extrapolate-the-pretrend test, so this is a real if modest capability.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming it stops with r(198) and its e(adversarial_*) results go (adversarial alone is unchanged), and the configs adv_altb and adv_r2001 with their baselines retire or are re-pointed at the primary test.

candidates.what_it_is: Turns off wooldid's program-scoped `set emptycells drop`, so the underlying regression carries columns for empty interaction cells.
candidates.why_delete: It changes no number (probe: e(b) and e(V) mreldif 0, 7.1 s vs 37.9 s, so about 5x slower rather than the 'roughly doubles' the help says), and the help itself says it is only of interest with verbose; a user wanting the raw regression reruns the verbose-printed command under `set emptycells keep`. The code is small, so the payoff is help and forwarding surface; the burden lens and the blue-sky review kept it as the escape hatch for a global Stata setting wooldid changes.
candidates.what_breaks: A do-file naming emptycellsoverride stops with r(198); nothing else changes.

candidates.what_it_is: Scalars carrying exactly the same two numbers as e(perm_bandlo_*) and e(perm_bandhi_*), documented in the help as deprecated aliases.
candidates.why_delete: They duplicate the canonical band scalars on every run (ado 310-313), and permute() is not in the v1.3 tag, so no do-file written for a tagged release can rely on them. Deleting them reverses your 2026-09-07 keep-with-deprecation ruling (CS-57/58); e(permdist) and e(boot_percentile_mainresults) were checked and are not pure aliases, so they stay.
candidates.what_breaks: Code reading e(perm_lb_*)/e(perm_ub_*) gets a missing value and must switch to e(perm_bandlo_*)/e(perm_bandhi_*), and the replay footer at ado 13235 must be re-pointed the same way.

rejected.why_kept: Heavy (about 300 lines, a jackknife loop), but it is the only BCa route when the user has aweights or pweights: the help says the bootstrap prefix refuses weights (sthlp 958), and the author has ruled on its display twice on 09-22.

mdt_wald, the GLS pre-trend slope and the implied bias have no counterpart in Roth's pretrends package (only mdt_nis overlaps, cross-checked to 2.5e-4), and the one-call bootstrap-covariance version is real capability the author built (F7) and ruled on repeatedly.
For a binary treatment gteffects supersedes it, but under contreat() (where gteffects is refused) it is the only in-package view of the cohort-level ame_i distribution.
A user-built unweighted lattice would not re-bin on each bootstrap replication, which is exactly the behaviour the author ruled 'Fix it' and built on 09-23 (a977d58).
It keeps the main-table SEs while skipping the expensive plot-cell margins SEs, which fastnose cannot do, and the author chose its engine behaviour in four 09-22 rulings.
Memory and estimation-stability routes bound up with the poisson paths the author ruled on 09-23/24; ccc_absorb is the memory route for many continuous coarse controls.
Five lines with no interactions, and it is the package's distribution channel; net install is a route, but the saving is negligible.

Not pure aliases: e(permdist) holds per-estimand draws on the e(perm_stat) scale (the t-ratio under permtstat), unlike e(permdist_b), and boot_percentile_mainresults makes the table name derivable from e(boot_display) under the default (ado 11159-11166).
Real burden, but it is the only route to HC2/HC3 and other regress vce() forms, and its collapse eligibility was built on 09-22 (cd46002).
